title: Introduce delegated token channel and unified refresh for pull/push streams (ergonomic parity)
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: There has been persistent cross-SDK divergence in how streaming consumers handle credential refresh and retries, resulting in token rotation races, duplicated refresh attempts, and awkward ergonomics when migrating examples between TypeScript, Go, and Python. This PR introduces a delegated token channel abstraction in the TypeScript SDK that matches the semantics we iterated on in Go/Python: single-flight refresh, lease-window proactive refresh, and explicit channel handoff for pull and push style streams. Summary of changes: 1) src/auth/delegated_channel.ts: new DelegatedTokenChannel class that accepts a user-provided async refresh handler and exposes a lightweight getToken()/invalidate() API optimized for streaming hot-paths. 2) src/stream/pullstream_adapter.ts and src/stream/pushstream_adapter.ts: adapters updated to consume DelegatedTokenChannel; removed inline refresh logic and consolidated retry logic into a shared stream/retry shim. 3) src/client/stream_client.ts: ergonomic convenience helpers StreamClient.openPullStreamWithDelegatedRefresh() and openPushStreamWithDelegatedRefresh() to reduce boilerplate for common patterns. 4) docs/auth/stream-credential-flow.md: documented the new pattern and migration notes. 5) tests/integration/stream_token_rotation.test.ts: deterministic test harness that simulates short-lived tokens and asserts single-flight refresh under concurrent consumers. 6) package.json bumped to 0.8.0 to reflect API additions. Compatibility and migration: The DelegatedTokenChannel is fully backward compatible with existing tokenProvider callback patterns but is recommended for streaming workloads. We maintained the legacy token callback wrapper (deprecated) and added deprecation warnings for one release cycle. Performance: stream hot-paths were benchmarked; added microbench in perf/bench_stream_token_hotpath.ts showing ~8% lower allocs and ~6% lower p95 latency when using delegated channel due to removed promise duplication. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed with SDK owners (ENG-9345) - [x] Type-safe APIs with TS declarations and JSDoc - [x] Integration tests covering race conditions - [x] Docs and quickstart updated - [x] Version bump and changelog entry - [x] CI green after two reruns Test notes: initial CI run showed a flaky integration test that reproduced locally when environment timeouts were aggressive; adjusted harness timing and re-ran full suite. Observability: added telemetry events auth.refresh.requested/auth.refresh.completed for monitoring refresh count per-client to make regressions visible in Console. Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature-flag default-on for SDK 0.8.x; recommend library consumers to adopt DelegatedTokenChannel for streaming jobs and migrate examples. Related: aligns TypeScript behavior with redwood-sdk-go@v1.5.3 and redwood-sdk-python@0.12.4 token lease semantics.

release_notes: TypeScript SDK 0.8.0: Introduces DelegatedTokenChannel for streaming credential refresh, ergonomic StreamClient helpers for pull/push streams, improved single-flight token refresh semantics to avoid duplicate refreshes under concurrency, performance improvements on stream hot-path, and telemetry for auth refresh events. Backward compatible; legacy token callback wrapper deprecated for one release.
